QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_16

question.text: For Cat III AIFs, continuing interest by Sponsor or Investment Manager must be not less than:

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower
2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is higher
5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is lower
10% of corpus or INR 20 crore, whichever is lower

explanation.text: The Logic: CTR row on Continuing Interest: Cat III AIFs require 5% of corpus OR INR 10 crore, WHICHEVER IS LOWER. (Cat I/II: 2.5% / INR 5 crore, whichever is lower.) This is the single most-tested Cat III vs Cat I/II discriminator. The Trap: Options A and B are Cat I/II numbers. Option D invents a higher threshold. The 'whichever is LOWER' qualifier is also a common swap-trap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests 2.5% / INR 5 cr for Cat I/II. XIX-C / XIX-E test the contrast. XIX-B (Cat III distributor) surfaces it at client level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III sponsor commit is SIZEABLE — at INR 200 cr corpus, the 5% rule binds (INR 10 cr); above INR 200 cr, the INR 10 cr cap binds. Plan sponsor funding in the launch timeline because the CTR annually tests continuing interest.
